title: A 2 percent inflation target is not one object: the Fed, the ECB, the Bank of Canada, and the Riksbank name different indexes
summary: A 2 percent inflation target is not one object: the Fed, the ECB, the Bank of Canada, and the Riksbank name different indexes.
body: Four official targets opened for this pack use the number 2 percent and do not use the same index. The FOMC's January 2026 statement uses the price index for personal consumption expenditures. The ECB uses the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices. The Bank of Canada uses the total consumer price index and places 2 percent as the midpoint of a 1 to 3 percent range. The Riksbank uses the CPIF. Section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act names stable prices and does not state 2 percent. The source says: "The Committee reaffirms its judgment that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve’s statutory maximum employment and price stability mandates." Comparing the slogans without the index compares different measurements. This card does not say which index is the right one.
